title: Auto Loans: interest owed through the credit date of a catch-up installment payment
content:
# Auto Loans: interest owed through the credit date of a catch-up installment payment

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower pays the earliest past-due installment of an auto loan by a transfer from the borrower's own PCB checking account. It fixes the interest owed on the day the payment is credited.

## Clause

The interest owed is the principal balance recomputed from the loan's ledger, multiplied by the loan's APR, divided by 100, divided by the product's day-count basis, multiplied by the number of calendar days from the last payment date (not counted) through the credit date (counted). It is rounded half-up to the cent **once**, on the final interest figure only.

## Counting the days

| Last payment date | Credit date | Days counted |
|---|---|---|
| 2027-01-20 | 2027-02-06 | 17 (January 21 to 31 is 11, February 1 to 6 is 6) |
| 2027-02-05 | 2027-02-06 | 1 |

## Rounding witness (hypothetical figures)

Suppose the unrounded interest for one day works out at 3.715093 and 17 days are counted.

| Method | Figure | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 17 times 3.715093 is 63.156581, rounded once | 63.16 | correct |
| Round the daily figure to 3.72 first, then 17 times 3.72 | 63.24 | wrong: rounding happens only on the final figure |

## Points of judgement

**Is the last payment date itself counted?** No. Counting starts the day after it and runs through the credit date, which is counted.

**Which balance bears the interest?** The principal balance as recomputed from the loan's ledger, at the loan's recorded APR.
